title: Metamorphoses - Book I, Creation and Flood
author: Publius Ovidius Naso
description: Ovid's poem of transformations, opening with the creation of the world from Chaos.

sections.latin:
In nova fert animus mutatas dicere formas
corpora; di, coeptis (nam vos mutastis et illas)
adspirate meis primaque ab origine mundi
ad mea perpetuum deducite tempora carmen!
sections.translation: My mind moves me to tell of forms changed into new bodies; gods, favor my undertaking (for you have changed even those forms), and from the first origin of the world lead down my continuous song to my own times!

lineByLine.latin: In nova fert animus mutatas dicere formas
lineByLine.translation: My mind moves me to tell of forms changed into new
lineByLine.notes: in nova...corpora: hyperbaton (separation of adjective and noun)

lineByLine.latin: corpora; di, coeptis (nam vos mutastis et illas)
lineByLine.translation: bodies; gods, favor my undertakings (for you have changed even those forms)
lineByLine.notes: di = dei; coeptis: dative plural with adspirate

lineByLine.latin: adspirate meis primaque ab origine mundi
lineByLine.translation: breathe upon my [work] and from the first origin of the world

lineByLine.latin: ad mea perpetuum deducite tempora carmen!
lineByLine.translation: lead down my continuous song to my own times!
lineByLine.notes: deducite: metaphor from spinning thread; perpetuum carmen: unbroken song

sections.latin:
Ante mare et terras et quod tegit omnia caelum
unus erat toto naturae vultus in orbe,
quem dixere chaos: rudis indigestaque moles
nec quicquam nisi pondus iners congestaque eodem
non bene iunctarum discordia semina rerum.
sections.translation: Before the sea and lands and the sky that covers all, nature had one face throughout the whole world, which they called Chaos: a rough and unformed mass, nothing except inert weight and discordant seeds of things not well joined, heaped together in the same place.

sections.latin:
Sanctius his animal mentisque capacius altae
deerat adhuc et quod dominari in cetera posset:
natus homo est, sive hunc divino semine fecit
ille opifex rerum, mundi melioris origo,
sive recens tellus seductaque nuper ab alto...
sections.translation: A holier creature than these, more capable of high mind, was still lacking, one that could rule over the rest: man was born—whether that craftsman of things, the origin of a better world, made him from divine seed, or whether the fresh earth, recently separated from the high heaven...

historicalContext: Ovid's Metamorphoses, completed around 8 CE, tells myths of transformation from creation to Julius Caesar's deification. It became one of the most influential works of classical literature, inspiring artists and writers for two millennia.
literaryFeatures: Epic scope with elegiac wit and irony
Philosophical cosmogony drawing on Greek sources
